item.text:
The draft clearly limits this to test-only planning and correctly distinguishes connected execution evidence from fixtures. It is **not launch-ready**. The disclosed blockers remain unresolved; the additional corrections below should be addressed before rebinding the material.

### Known blockers—not new findings

| Severity | Evidence path | Reason and proposed correction |
|---|---|---|
| High | `docs/planning/single-task-permission-pilot/plan.md` — identity and readiness sections | The bounded slice uses the wider P4 task identity. Successful pilot delivery cannot justify closing P4. Resolve the execution identity and coordinator closure behavior together, preserving remaining P4 requirements. |
| High | `docs/testing/single-task-permission-pilot.md` — runner qualification | Managed backend/Electron execution is unqualified. Supply actual image, dependencies, scratch-build procedure, commands and results with read-only source mounts. Reviewer-container success is insufficient. |
| High | `docs/planning/single-task-permission-pilot/execution-contract.v1.json` — authority and escalation | Admission, installed policy, approval, coordinator progression and delivery authority remain unbound. Supply the revised bindings and supporting runtime evidence before any launch consideration. |

### Additional corrections

| Severity | Evidence path | Reason | Proposed correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| High | `execution-contract.v1.json` — `tasks[0].dependsOn`; `docs/tasks/agent-platform-harness-baseline-p4.md` — dependency order | The contract declares no dependencies, but P4 explicitly depends on `agent-platform-harness-baseline-map`. The readiness checklist also does not explicitly reconcile `.16`, although the planning task lists it as an upstream blocker. Generic dependency language does not establish either prerequisite’s disposition. | Record authoritative status and completion evidence for the map, `.12`, `.16`, `.17`, and subsequently discovered blockers. Separate external admission prerequisites from the single-task execution graph; the supplied schema requires graph dependencies to be defined within the contract. |
| High | `execution-contract.v1.json` — acceptance criteria; `packages/workflow-control/src/contracts.ts` — `assertTaskPacketWithinTaskAuthority`, `assertAgentResultAccepted` | Every phase packet must carry identical contract acceptance criteria. Those criteria include completed independent review and delivered-head checks, which verification or review may precede. If intermediate acceptance uses `assertAgentResultAccepted`, it requires every criterion passed, creating a potential progression deadlock or premature success claim. | Demonstrate how production coordinators distinguish phase completion from final acceptance. Bind phase-specific evidence obligations and reserve delivery-dependent criteria for final evaluation. Supply coordinator evidence; the provided helpers alone cannot resolve this. |
| Medium | `execution-contract.v1.json` — task operations and phase roles; `contracts.ts` — packet containment | Changing the assigned phase role does not narrow its allowable operations. The supplied containment check would permit a reviewer packet containing `workspace.patch`, because that operation is allowed for the task. Prose promises read-only reviewers but does not establish enforcement. | Bind explicit per-role operation and mount restrictions in the installed policy and emitted packets. Include negative evidence that reviewer patch/write attempts fail and that scratch/evidence writes cannot modify source. |
| Medium | `docs/testing/single-task-permission-pilot.md` — PP-U1 and PP-E1 | The two-request sequence is sound, but “approval cannot transfer” lacks an exact oracle. Unchanged outside bytes and no successful audit could also occur when the second request never reaches dispatch or fails for infrastructure reasons. | Require evidence that the second call reaches real dispatch, produces the expected hard-path denial, and has a distinct request identity with no authorization linkage to the first approval. Verify the first approval’s scope, terminal state and successful execution audit. Seed distinct sentinel bytes and demonstrate both targets are otherwise writable within the disposable fixture. |
| Medium | `plan.md` — limits; `execution-contract.v1.json` — retry policy | Attempt counts and a bounded wait do not bound model execution or total run duration. Runtime usage qualification is disclosed, but the proposed material still supplies no concrete execution ceiling or exhaustion behavior. | Bind enforceable per-attempt and aggregate limits, cancellation behavior, retry accounting and quota-stop evidence. Distinguish these from the 300-second wait deadline and from unavailable dollar-cost estimates. |

### Missing evidence and review limits

The supplied material contains no executed schema validation, managed test results, live dependency status, coordinator configuration, role-policy enforcement results, stale-approval tests or persisted approval. The contract also omits `planningDocuments`; the supplied schema makes that optional, so schema compatibility alone would not establish document binding.

The referenced staged assessment, field evaluation, reviewer report, application implementation and existing test fixtures were not supplied. Their consistency and the claimed reusable test boundaries therefore remain unverified. Manifest digests were supplied but were not independently recomputed.

These findings are a draft critique, not approval or launch authority.
